title: Programmable Asymmetric Spin-Orbit Torque Switching for Spin Logic
authors: Rongkun Han, Dahai Wei, Jianhua Zhao, Yuan Lu
abstract: Spin logic devices provide a promising route toward ultralow-power and nonvolatile information processing. In this work, we demonstrate field-free spin-orbit torque-induced asymmetric magnetization switching in in-plane anisotropy (IMA) and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy heterostructures, characterized by different critical switching currents under opposite current polarities. Combined experiments and macrospin simulations reveal that the asymmetric switching originates from an in-plane effective field Hy , which breaks the Myz mirror symmetry of the system. By controlling the magnetization direction of the IMA layer, both the switching polarity and bias direction can be tuned. Building on four distinct types of asymmetric switching behaviors, we realize a reconfigurable spin logic operation within a single Hall-bar device. These results clarify the physical origin of asymmetric magnetization switching and demonstrate an approach for realizing reconfigurable spin logic devices.
summary: This research demonstrates how to achieve programmable, field-free, and asymmetric magnetization switching in magnetic multilayers using Spin-Orbit Torque. The asymmetry is fundamentally linked to an internal effective magnetic field ($H_y$) that breaks system symmetry. By controlling this asymmetry based on the initial magnetization state, the authors successfully realize a reconfigurable spin logic device.
main_problem: The work aims to demonstrate and understand programmable, field-free, asymmetric spin-orbit torque (SOT)-induced magnetization switching for realizing reconfigurable spin logic devices.
main_result: Asymmetric switching is shown to originate from an in-plane effective field ($H_y$) that breaks system symmetry, enabling the realization of programmable spin logic by controlling the initial magnetization state.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (SQUID, magnetotransport, pulsed current switching) with theoretical modeling using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation.
model_or_system: The physical system is an Fe/Mn2CoAl(MCA)/Pt multilayer heterostructure grown on GaAs(001). The dynamics are modeled using the LLG equation, incorporating SOT torques and effective in-plane anisotropy fields ($H_x, H_y$).
key_observables: Critical switching currents (different for opposite polarities), magnetization hysteresis loops, and the resulting Boolean logic output states ($R_{xy}$ vs. pulse number).
important_parameters: The asymmetry is governed by the internal effective field $H_y$, while the switching polarity is controlled by the initial magnetization direction of the IMA layer.
main_assumptions: The asymmetry is attributed to intrinsic symmetry breaking by the magnetic field, ruling out Joule heating effects. The logic inputs are encoded via current pulses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the multilayer stack, M-H curves showing switching, symmetry schematics detailing the role of $H_y$, and finally, a truth table demonstrating the realization of multiple Boolean logic gates.
paper_structure: The paper first characterizes the material's in-plane magnetic anisotropy using PHE measurements. It then investigates SOT switching, establishing that the asymmetry is due to $H_y$. Finally, it leverages this tunable asymmetry across four initial magnetization states to implement a full set of programmable spin logic operations.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the concept of symmetry breaking via an internal effective field ($H_y$) to control non-linear switching behavior is analogous to controlling non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems or engineered quantum potentials.
